extDesc.message: On any Wikipedia article, see which language version is most complete, ranked by prose depth and reference count.

ssRanking.message: How Wikiweigher decides the best language.

ssDisplay.message: Theme, accent color, and the card's language.

ssReading.message: Languages you read, and where the card shows.

ssSupport.message: What happened on the last run, and how to report a problem.

noteCompleteness.message: How many languages get exact word and reference counts (6 / 12 / 24). More is more thorough but slower. Changing it re-ranks the open article right away.

noteCardLanguage.message: Auto uses the article's language for the card's own labels.

noteLanguagesYouRead.message: Comma-separated codes. If the best language is not one you read, the card offers a translate link. On articles with many language versions these codes also help decide which get measured. Left empty, your browser's languages are used.

noteDrag.message: Drag the card by its header to move it - it remembers where you left it.

noteReportPrivacy.message: The wiki and the article title, never the full page address or your history.

noteSettingsData.message: Import checks every value before applying it.

noteRate.message: A quick review helps other readers find it.

confirmReset.message: Reset every Wikiweigher setting to its default?

confirmOverflow.message: The report is too long to put in the link, so it will be copied to your clipboard instead. Paste it into the Diagnostics field on the issue page. Copy it now?

noteReportPick.message: Two ways in. Both send the same details, already filled in.

wayGithubNote.message: Needs a GitHub account. Public, and you get notified when it is fixed.

wayEmailNote.message: No account needed. Opens your mail app with the report written for you.

msgMailFallback.message: Diagnostics copied and saved as a file. Attach or paste it into the email.

msgMailFallbackFile.message: Diagnostics saved as a file. Attach it to the email.

aboutBlurb.message: Ranks the same Wikipedia article across its languages and recommends the most complete one to read.
